data.description:
We are making a web image maker. This is a software with two modes. It could be a web app or desktop software, discuss with me about which is best.

Main menu: typical eye dropper, pen, line, and shape tools, color selector etc. appear above the main UI. On the left, we have a 3x3 grid. on the right, we have rendered output.

Mode 1: Border image.
Output: Images that can be used as css border-images. These are square images, that are understood within the css rules as a 3x3 grid, with an empty middle section
UI: a 3x3 square grid. configurable pixel size. draw in each section, and rendered examples appear to the side for each of the border-image style rules


Mode 2: Repeating background image
Output: images that will be tiled, for example in the context of css background-images
UI: 3x3 square grid, with the middle section being the implied main drawing canvas. All grid boxes can be drawn in. Delineation is faint. drawing in this adds what's being drawn to the other sections as well, and the user can draw a line from one box to another.



Typical UX patterns of drawing software should be present, hotkeys, etc
data.title: Scaffold pattern making software

data.body: Interview decisions (human-confirmed): platform=web app (Tauri wrap possible later); canvas=zoomed pixel editor, configurable cell size ~8-64px; stack=Vite + vanilla TypeScript, no framework; outputs=PNG export + copyable CSS snippet (border-image shorthand / background tile, data-URI image) + project save/load (localStorage autosave + JSON file). Mode semantics confirmed: mode 1 = border-image slice editor, center cell locked/empty, live previews of stretch/repeat/round; mode 2 = single tile drawn on torus, all 9 cells show same tile, strokes wrap across edges. UI follows BRANDING.md (pattern maker PM-1, teenage-engineering idiom).

Implementation complete across all 7 phases (commits 6e39957..e30b107): vite+strict-ts scaffold with PM-1 device shell; PixelBuffer/raster core (Bresenham, rect, ellipse, wrap-aware flood fill with visited set); doc model with locked border center + torus tile plotting; per-mode snapshot undo/redo (cap 64); full 7-tool set with hotkeys and alt-pick; tile mode (mode bank, keys 1/2, faint delineation); live previews (4 real border-image boxes at 158px, tile swatches 1x/4x, 150ms debounce off the pointermove path) + css clipboard + pattern.png; strict pattern.json persistence with localStorage autosave and undoable import; cell stepper 8-64 with undoable resample; welcome mark; reduced-motion/focus-visible respected. Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, npm run build green, 55-check node smoke run over the DOM-free modules (torus flood termination+wrap, center-lock walls, true-modulo plotting, undo across resize, corrupt-file rejection, slice math) — smoke script was throwaway in scratchpad, not committed. Deviations: (1) flood fill is a 4-neighbor visited-set stack fill, not literal scanline spans — same signature/behavior, simpler to prove correct under wrap, negligible cost at <=192px; (2) plan left cellSize-change undo semantics across per-mode stacks unspecified — resizes push snapshots to BOTH stacks and restoring an entry with a different cellSize resamples the other mode's buffer to keep the doc invariant; (3) added tools/shape.ts (shared drag-shape machinery) beyond the listed files; (4) ellipse uses symmetric quarter-arc sampling instead of classic midpoint (exact 4-way symmetry incl. half-integer centers); (5) eraser tip reworded for transparency semantics; (6) base64 codec hand-rolled (no btoa) to keep raster/ portable. NOT verified (no browser here): plan section-8 by-hand items — HiDPI crispness, real clipboard/download UX, border-image rendering across browsers. Reviewer should npm run dev and walk acceptance criteria 2-12.
